question: Should OpenClaw permit `gateway.auth.mode: "none"` on non-loopback or private-ingress Gateway binds, and what explicit guardrail or acknowledgement is required if it does?
rationale: The current implementation intentionally blocks reachable unauthenticated Gateway startup, while the request would move operator-surface protection from OpenClaw auth to external network controls.

options.title: Keep fail-closed default
options.body: Preserve the current token/password/trusted-proxy requirement for reachable Gateway binds and direct deployments to the existing delegated-auth path.

options.title: Sponsor guarded private-ingress mode
options.body: Allow no-auth reachable binds only behind a deliberately named high-risk policy with startup warnings, audit findings, documentation, and focused tests.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: Reject this trust model in core and explain the supported token/password and trusted-proxy alternatives.

recommendation.title: Keep fail-closed default
recommendation.body: Preserve the current token/password/trusted-proxy requirement for reachable Gateway binds and direct deployments to the existing delegated-auth path.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is tied to recent Gateway auth hardening and was explicitly mentioned in the issue timeline for the auth-boundary decision.
